Immortality kills me

thoughts of dieing, it thrills me

but I can’t so I won’t

but I shall go on hunting, looking

poking, searching- who am I?

I’m this poem.

 

letters are thickets of my inspiration

words; implosions of my passionary reactionary

lines pigments of my orientation

the stanza, my monolithic semantic slaughter

it is my world, a quasi-life without the living

where poppies are black

and violets are grey as far as the eye can see

the lakes in my world have no consequence

everything is illusory- fantasy

raining chards of granite cut through me

sparks fly with every impact

and the swords are everywhere

cutting, slicing, dicing.

 

You the reader are devourers of my poetic endeavor

analogous feelings

like any explosions- big bang singulars

viral diseases I’m spreading

I’m stuck here forever

Boiled eggs are one of my favorites and they're really easy. They also will keep in the refrigerator in a Tupperware container for at least 2 or 3 days before the flavor starts to fall off.

First, you want older eggs that are near or slightly past the sell by date. Fresh eggs are a lot harder to peel.

Place them in a saucepan and cover with water until it is a couple inches (5-6cm) over the top of the eggs. Turn the heat on to high. Once the water starts a rolling boil (bubbles are constantly coming off the bottom of the pot) turn off the heat and let the eggs sit in the boiling water for 10 minutes. Take one egg out of the water (a large slotted spoon works well for this), hit it with the back of a spoon to put a crack in it and then run it under cold water from the tap in order to cool it off enough to peel.

Peel it, cut it open and check to see how done the yolk is. It should be done or at least pretty close to it. You want the yolk to be completely solid, but still a yellow or orange color. If it is runny, it is not done yet. If it has any green tint to it, you have overcooked the egg. The green color comes from sulfur compounds breaking down and it gives the eggs an off flavor that you do not want.

If your eggs are not done, allow them to sit in the hot water for a while longer (5-7 min) and then check again. If they are done, prepare a large bowl of ice water and crack each egg slightly with a strike from the back of a spoon then throw it in the ice water. This causes the shell to peel away from the egg and makes it much easier to remove. It also cools it and makes it easier to handle. Remove the eggs from the ice water to peel them. Running water from the tap over the egg while peeling will assist in the process.

That should be detailed enough that you can figure it out.

Pro tip for checking if your boiled eggs are done: Take it out of the boiling pot and spin it on the counter. Quickly touch the spinning egg with your finger, just enough to stop it from spinning. If the yolk is still runny, the inertia will cause the egg to keep moving. If the yolk is hard, it will stay still because its inertia is gone.

But at that point where it's about 90% done, this doesn't really work. It will still stop spinning, but when you cut it open it can still be slightly under cooked. The yolk becomes solid a bit before it is completely cooked.
This is exactly what I was looking for. My parents used to boil eggs but never used any techniques for making them easier to peel.

The main key is using older eggs. The membrane sac inside starts to pull away from the shell and that makes them far easier to peel. The cold shock helps do the same. It causes the membrane to shrink away from the shell.
